definitions.explanation: A form of government in which a single person (king, queen, emperor) serves as head of state. Can be absolute (unlimited power) or constitutional (power limited by a constitution).

examples.japanese: イギリスは{君主制|くんしゅせい}の{国|くに}だ。
{多|おお}くの{国|くに}が{君主制|くんしゅせい}から{共和制|きょうわせい}に{移行|いこう}した。
examples.english: Many countries transitioned from monarchy to a republic.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}は{立憲君主制|りっけんくんしゅせい}に{分類|ぶんるい}されることがある。
examples.english: Japan is sometimes classified as a constitutional monarchy.

notes:
Composed of {君主|くんしゅ} (monarch, sovereign) + {制|せい} (system). The suffix {制|せい} is productive and attaches to nouns to describe political, social, or organizational systems.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立憲君主制|りっけんくんしゅせい}: constitutional monarchy
- {絶対君主制|ぜったいくんしゅせい}: absolute monarchy
- {君主制|くんしゅせい}を{廃止|はいし}する: to abolish monarchy
- {君主制|くんしゅせい}{国家|こっか}: monarchical state

RELATED WORDS:
- {共和制|きょうわせい}: republic (contrasting system)
- {独裁制|どくさいせい}: dictatorship
- {民主制|みんしゅせい}: democracy
- {天皇制|てんのうせい}: emperor system (Japan-specific)
